page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a general-purpose cloud compute instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture, comprising 8 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with two threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). Storage consists of a bundled 960 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance lacks dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core performance alongside dependable multi-core execution. The processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3622.78) as well as data compression and decompression tasks, including single-threaded gzip compression at 39.34 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.66 GB/sec. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. This capability enables high text generation speeds on smaller language models (443.84 tokens/sec on 135M parameters) and strong memory throughput, scoring 2803.28 in PassMark memory testing.

Across aggregate multi-threaded benchmarks, the instance demonstrates mid-range throughput, recording a multi-core stress-ng score of 28925.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11775.0. Redis SET operations reach 31.26 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 41.41 GB/sec. With its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe capacity, the server provides cost-effective efficiency for general application workloads, production web servers, caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and transactional database tasks without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware.
description: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute line. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core stress-ng performance and fast single-threaded compression speeds, complemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptographic acceleration. Multi-threaded metrics settle squarely in the mid-range across PassMark and Geekbench test suites, with Redis SET performance delivering 31.26 million operations per second. The balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio and fast bundled storage make this instance appropriate for relational databases, continuous integration build nodes, caching systems, and general production enterprise backends.
